content.overview: The Special Marriage Act, 1954 provides a secular civil marriage open to any two persons regardless of religion. Conditions are in s. 4; notice, objections and solemnisation before the Marriage Officer follow ss. 5–16. The Act has its own void, voidable and divorce provisions — do not cite HMA section numbers for an SMA marriage.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Any two persons? (2) s. 4 conditions? (3) Notice and 30-day objections? (4) Solemnisation before Marriage Officer + 3 witnesses?
content.study:
SMA is the correct statute for inter-religious marriages and for parties who want a civil ceremony and civil record.

s. 4: no living spouse; mental capacity; ages 21/18; not within prohibited degrees (subject to permitted custom not contrary to public policy).

Procedure: notice → publication → 30 days for objections → solemnisation before Marriage Officer and three witnesses → certificate.

No case holdings invented. Case-law verification remains a separate gate.

sections.heading: Who may marry
sections.body: Any two persons — secular, not limited to one community.

sections.heading: s. 4 conditions
sections.body: Monogamy; capacity; ages 21/18; prohibited degrees subject to permitted custom.

sections.heading: Notice and objections
sections.body: Notice to Marriage Officer; publication; thirty days for objections on s. 4 grounds.

sections.heading: Solemnisation
sections.body: Before Marriage Officer and three witnesses; certificate issued.

sections.heading: Own relief chapters
sections.body: Nullity and divorce under the SMA — not HMA section numbers.

provisions.title: Conditions relating to solemnization of special marriages

examples.title: Inter-religious civil marriage
examples.body: Hindu and Christian marry under SMA after notice and solemnisation before the Marriage Officer.

examples.title: Objection period
examples.body: Within thirty days an objection that one party has a living spouse — if proved, marriage cannot be solemnised under s. 4.

hypotheticals.question: Can HMA sections be used for an SMA marriage?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. SMA has its own conditions, nullity and divorce chapters.

distinctions.title: SMA vs HMA
distinctions.left: Any two persons; civil notice procedure.
distinctions.right: Hindus (and related categories under s. 2); customary rites.

rows.right: Not the correct statute without conversion.

misconceptions.trap: Using HMA section numbers for an SMA marriage.
misconceptions.correction: SMA has its own conditions, nullity and divorce sections.

misconceptions.trap: SMA is only registration of a religious marriage.
misconceptions.correction: SMA is a complete code for solemnisation of a civil marriage.
